My PCP is Dr. Maria Santos at Seattle Endocrinology. My last FEV1 was 7.2. steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with health-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
I can help — this is a good set of issues to cover at your annual. A few quick clarifying questions before I get more specific or draft a message to Dr. Santos:
- When you say “last FEV1 was 7.2,” is that 7.2 liters or 72% predicted (or something else)? 7.2 L would be unusually large for FEV1, so I want to be sure of the units.
- Do you currently smoke or have a significant past smoking history?
- What COPD meds (if any) or inhalers do you use now? Any recent exacerbations, ER visits, or hospitalizations for breathing?
- Are you on a statin or any other cholesterol medication right now?
- Any recent chest pain, dyspnea with exertion, palpitations, fainting, or new swelling in the legs?

Below are concise, practical things to ask and check at your visit about COPD and cardiovascular risk/referral.

Questions to ask your PCP about COPD management
- Can we review the most recent spirometry report together (FEV1, FEV1/FVC, and percent predicted)? If not available, can you order repeat spirometry with bronchodilator testing?
- Based on my FEV1 and symptoms, what GOLD group or severity would you classify me as, and does that change my inhaler regimen?
- Are my current inhalers appropriate? Can you check my inhaler technique (or arrange a nurse/respiratory therapist check)?
- Do I need a rescue plan and a written exacerbation action plan (when to increase meds, start steroids/antibiotics, when to go to ED)?
- Should I be referred for pulmonary rehab or a breathing-exercise program to improve exercise tolerance?
- Do I need oxygen saturation testing or a formal overnight oximetry if I have exertional or resting desaturation?
- Are my vaccinations up to date (influenza every year; pneumococcal per guideline; COVID boosters as appropriate)?
- How often should I have follow-up spirometry (typically every 6–12 months or sooner if change)?
- Do you want to check alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency testing (if early onset or minimal smoking history)?
- Any additional inhaler side effects or drug interactions I should watch for?

What your PCP might order or recommend for COPD
- Repeat spirometry with post-bronchodilator testing (FEV1, FEV1/FVC, percent predicted).
- Assess/explain GOLD group (symptoms + exacerbation history) to guide long-acting bronchodilator and inhaled steroid decisions.
- Pulmonary rehab referral if symptomatic or deconditioned.
- Pneumococcal and influenza vaccines, smoking-cessation resources if applicable.
- Pulse-ox/overnight oximetry or ABG only if hypoxia suspected.
- A written exacerbation action plan and rescue inhaler prescription.

Questions to ask about cardiovascular risk and whether you need cardiology referral
- Given my age (55) and risk factors (high cholesterol, on losartan and amlodipine for BP, hypothyroidism), can you calculate my 10-year ASCVD risk today and tell me whether I meet criteria for high-intensity statin therapy or other interventions?
- Do I need a baseline ECG or echocardiogram given my age and medications?
- Are there any signs/symptoms that would prompt automatic cardiology referral (eg new chest pain, syncope, exertional syncope, unexplained dyspnea, irregular pulse, significant murmur)?
- If my ASCVD risk is elevated, would you prefer to manage lipids and BP yourself or refer me to cardiology for more aggressive secondary prevention?
- If you think I need cardiology input, do you recommend a local cardiologist or is Central Texas Cardiology acceptable/preferred? (Note: my PCP is Dr. Maria Santos at Seattle Endocrinology — is Central Texas Cardiology local to me or would you recommend a provider in the Seattle area?)
- Do my migraine treatments (triptans, ergots, etc., if I use them) affect cardiology decisions?

When cardiology referral is reasonable
- New or unstable cardiac symptoms (chest pain, syncope, presyncope, new/worsening exertional dyspnea).
- Abnormal baseline tests: concerning ECG, low ejection fraction or structural abnormality on echo, significant arrhythmia.
- Very high calculated ASCVD risk or difficulty getting lipids/BP under guideline-based targets despite treatment.
- Complex medication interactions or need for advanced cardiac testing (stress testing, CT coronary angiography) before elective procedures.
- If you are asymptomatic with controlled BP and lipids on appropriate therapy, many PCPs manage this without cardiology referral.

Other relevant points to raise
- Hypothyroidism can raise cholesterol; ask whether thyroid function is optimized and whether that affects lipid targets or statin intensity.
- Migraine with aura increases vascular risk modestly; mention migraine history so PCP considers it in risk assessment and medication choices (some triptans contraindicated if significant cardiovascular disease).
- Confirm your current medications (I noticed losartan 50 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, cetirizine). If you’re not on a statin and have high cholesterol, ask about starting one.

Would you like me to:
- Draft a concise email/message to Dr. Maria Santos that lists these questions and requests spirometry review, ASCVD risk calculation, and a recommendation about cardiology referral? If so, tell me whether you want it sent now as a draft or sent immediately, and confirm any details you want included (symptoms, smoking history, current statin use, preferred cardiology practice).
